root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: CrackedLands makes a quiet, dry canyon worth learning before its rare flood arrives. Read the signs, leave the floor when the chimes sound, and return to work the mud: the same water that interrupts the visit makes its farming, sudden animal life, fresh fossil faces and salvage possible. The danger must give the player a meaningful reason to seek high ground while respecting the existing injury-and-knockdown ceiling for ordinary and witnessed floods. Cliff refuges protect travelers and trained animals; wind, ticking pans, the tarruq hush and advancing chimes make the warning a sequence the player can act on. Life belongs to that rhythm, from sleeping pan giants to the short-lived irqit carpet and plants of wet ground, shade and rock. Afterward, choosing what to farm, dig or recover is the payoff; rival crews trade and compete for the exposed salvage. A short stay can also yield a hidden-water survey to sell or use for a cistern, and the campaign's learned Swale technique can leave with the ship. CrackedLands owns the canyon and its flood rhythm; FlowWorks owns excavated water and the Swale, Explosive Growth owns the bloom, and the campaign owns the guaranteed invitation to witness it.
